facets.rationale: Invoke Plan is retained as the required subject because it governs the translation from an admitted Design into bounded implementation work and has a non-mutation authority ceiling.

The model independently represents Work Pack, delivery slice, implementation layer, wave, task, SWU, implementation detail, validation, gate, blocker, gap, execution entry, Execution Pack, closeout synchronization, and the conditional pre-execution prerequisite.
Containment and governance use child-to-parent depends-on relations, consumers and selectors reference source truth, and the choreography-only Execution Pack contrasts with Work Pack source truth.

The authoring source, candidate bundle, bundle admission, and Plan evidence state preserve authored, admitted, readiness-preflight, exact-acceptance, and execution-authority claims as distinct states.

Validation obligations, Plan gates, blockers, gaps, SWU atomicity, evidence-based layer promotion, Distill outcomes, closeout completeness, and readiness proof conditions remain independently testable.
Execution entry selects exactly one bounded unit, while closeout synchronization and any declared pre-execution owner prerequisite constrain mutation-capable handoff without performing execution.

Invoke owns Plan authoring and handoff context, consumes admitted Design meaning by reference, and excludes redesign, task execution, owner acceptance, lifecycle completion, promotion, publication, deployment, and mutation authority.

includes: The sole authored machine source for Work Pack meaning, finite frontier, routes, write and effect scopes, validation contracts, budgets, and readiness configuration.
excludes: Separately authored generated Work Pack views, derived WPRA configuration, calculated digests, validator decisions, owner acceptance, and execution receipts.
conditions: Exactly one source must bind the exact admitted Design predecessor and compile without semantic invention into the governed Plan projections.

includes: The complete generated Plan artifact inventory and its exact producer evidence.
excludes: Independent bundle admission, implementation readiness, exact owner acceptance, execution admission, task execution, and product mutation.
conditions: Every member must derive from the same exact Plan execution source and producer run.

includes: Independent replay, exact inventory comparison, predecessor freshness, structural checks, and declared consumer results for one candidate.
excludes: Semantic invention, Design revision, implementation-readiness proof, owner acceptance, execution authorization, and mutation.
conditions: Admission must be independently produced for the exact candidate and must not be inferred from candidate generation or a generic PASS.

includes: Separate authored, admitted, readiness-preflight, exact-acceptance, and execution-authority states with exact evidence references.
excludes: A collapsed readiness label, generic PASS, inferred acceptance, inferred registry release, inferred runtime readiness, and inferred permission to mutate.
conditions: Every positive state must be supported by current evidence from the owner of that state, and a positive earlier state must not imply a later one.

includes: Implementation objective, delivery boundary, decomposition, ordering, layer governance, validation, gates, blockers, gaps, closeout contract, evidence state, and execution handoff.
excludes: Reopening admitted Design decisions, editing upstream artifacts, implementing tasks, accepting product changes, lifecycle completion, promotion, publication, deployment, and mutation authority.
conditions: The Plan must bind one exact admitted Design predecessor and must stop when required planning inputs, companions, or acceptance-critical evidence are missing or contradictory.

includes: Objective, delivery slices, task and SWU manifests, validation strategy, blockers, gates, current state, finite frontier, execution policy, and navigation to owned split contracts.
excludes: Layer philosophy owned by Implementation Layering, duplicated deep task detail owned by useful split task files, and choreography presented as a second source of truth.
conditions: Split task, wave, and choreography views must agree with the Work Pack or its gate must block.

includes: One coherent delivered outcome and its evidence-based evaluation boundary.
excludes: Execution ordering, task-local instructions, and SWU atomicity.
conditions: Every delivery slice must map to one or more Plan tasks and have a validation strategy.

includes: One L0-L3 decision question, minimum working proof, included and deferred scope, exit evidence, promotion decision, and non-regression obligations.
excludes: Task implementation details, SWU contracts, task status, and execution choreography.
conditions: Promotion must cite evidence from the prior layer, preserve prior guarantees, and keep deferred scope explicit.

includes: Layer mapping, wave goal, ordered tasks and SWUs, entry gate, dependency order, safe parallelization boundary, and exit evidence.
excludes: Detailed algorithms and source-of-truth task or SWU definitions.
conditions: Wave ordering must respect task and SWU dependencies, and parallel units must have disjoint write scopes or an explicit merge plan.

includes: One implementation responsibility with objective, slice and layer mapping, dependencies, source context, scope, done criteria, validation, SWUs, handoff, synchronization, and completion evidence.
excludes: Global Plan rationale, unrelated task state, and title-only or outcome-only placeholders.
conditions: A task must belong to one or more waves, and a split task file must be a useful execution contract.

includes: One primary behavior or decision, exactly one parent task, explicit dependencies, bounded write scope, source anchors, done criteria, acceptance evidence, validation surface, owner recommendation, split analysis, and handoff context.
excludes: Multiple independently verifiable behaviors, regions, projections, interactions, or responsive concerns bundled for convenience.
conditions: The unit must have one independently reviewable acceptance boundary, must split when plausible child units can pass independently, and the first selected unit must be the narrowest reversible trust-building step.

includes: Purpose, inputs, outputs, data or state, algorithm or ordered steps, interfaces, data flow, precedence or transition rules, edge cases, failure modes, constraints, and validation evidence.
excludes: New product or architecture decisions that belong in Design and unrelated implementation choices.
conditions: Medium and high complexity execution tasks require this detail, and acceptance-critical missing detail blocks handoff.

includes: The exact target, validation phase, command or reviewable check, expected result, evidence output, and failure behavior.
excludes: Unrunnable aspirations, untyped shell prose, and future post-produce evidence represented as current pre-execution PASS.
conditions: Validation timing must match when its required artifact can exist and every delivery slice and non-exempt SWU must have applicable evidence.

includes: A named target, required evidence, accepted outcomes, decision, and blocker causes controlling layer, wave, task, Work Pack, or handoff advancement.
excludes: Implicit approval, preference-based promotion, and generic PASS without typed current evidence.
conditions: A positive decision requires all acceptance-critical evidence to be present, current, valid, and consistent; otherwise the affected transition must stop.

includes: The exact cause, affected unit or gate, causal dependencies, responsible owner, and repair route.
excludes: Non-blocking future improvement and an unowned vague concern.
conditions: While unresolved, the blocker must prevent its named current transition or claim.

includes: The missing item, current non-blocking rationale, owner, repair route, and escalation condition.
excludes: Any condition already preventing acceptance, readiness, or safe execution.
conditions: The current bounded claim must remain valid without the item, and the gap must escalate to a blocker when it becomes acceptance-critical.

includes: Exactly one selected task or SWU, its dependencies, route, target, write and effect scope, typed inputs, expected receipt, admission timing, evidence, current state, automatic decisions, and stop decisions.
excludes: Task execution, implicit unit or successor selection, undeclared routes, protected effects, broader mutation authority, promotion, publication, and deployment.
conditions: The selected unit and exact route projection must pass the installed entry checks; semantic choice, scope expansion, protected effects, or failed acceptance-critical validation must stop.

includes: Medium/high-complexity wave order, stage coverage, cross-task dependencies, closure obligations, and safe parallelization boundaries.
excludes: Work Pack source truth, source-of-truth task details, SWU definitions, and independent execution state.
conditions: Every referenced unit, dependency, and layer assignment must agree with the Work Pack graph and owned split contracts.

includes: The terminal source receipt contract, exact synchronization-target inventory, baseline binding, admitted delta classes, lifecycle-owner validation, expected owner receipt, and deterministic successor policy for one mutation-capable SWU.
excludes: Implementation admission, another SWU, authority changes, promotion, publication, deployment, destructive cleanup, cost or risk acceptance, and unrelated targets.
conditions: The contract must be complete before source mutation, targets must not be inferred after mutation, and any successor must be uniquely and deterministically selected from the declared Work Pack.

includes: The bound route, task, SWU, active attempt, target inventory, validation contracts, expected owner receipt, satisfaction predicate, authorization evidence, allowed effect, return-control handle, and resume point.
excludes: A bare Work Pack declaration as apply authority, execution admission, a generic outer-loop prerequisite, and creation of a second Task Session.
conditions: It exists only for an already resolved Task Session attempt, must return control to that same attempt, and may resume exactly once at task-session context build.

consumer_topology.no_consumers_evidence: The bounded current files are Plan contracts and authoring templates, while the allowed successor artifacts and completed prior package are historical semantic evidence. None independently declares itself a current downstream consumer of the new target:invoke-plan-successor semantic artifact. The expanded context's catalogued Goal/SWU mention is historical narrative evidence and was not promoted to a current consumer claim.
